meta.title: Support
meta.description: Where to ask about React Scheduler, what a useful bug report contains, how to report a vulnerability privately, and how long a version is supported.

ask.text: Questions go to <ext href="https://github.com/kiralygyula92/react-scheduler/discussions">GitHub Discussions</ext>: how to do something, whether a behavior is intended, whether an idea fits the package. Issues are for defects, so a question opened as an issue is usually moved there.

bug.intro: Open an <ext href="https://github.com/kiralygyula92/react-scheduler/issues/new">issue</ext> with these five things. A report that has them can usually be fixed the same day it is read; one that has none rarely moves at all.
points: The version of the package and of React, and the browser the problem appears in.
What you expected to happen, in one sentence.
What happened instead, in one sentence.
A minimal reproduction: the smallest <Scheduler> that still shows it, with its items inline. A link to a sandbox or a small repository is ideal.
Anything that makes it appear or disappear: a viewport width, a locale, the timeline rather than the list.
bug.reduce: Reducing the case is the part that helps most. Remove props until the problem goes away, and the last one you removed is usually in the title of the fix.

security.text: Report a vulnerability privately through the repository’s Security tab, not in a public issue. The report stays visible only to the maintainers until a fix is released; SECURITY.md in the repository says what to include and when to expect an answer.

policy.text: Fixes land on the latest minor release of the current major, and that release is the one documented here. While the package is below 1.0.0 there is one supported version at a time — the latest. What that means for upgrades is on the Versions page.
